clue.text: Company in pub team regard as thoughtless

indicators.note: the company abbreviation sits inside the word for a pub, splitting it open

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a side is a team
to rate something is to regard or esteem it

explanation.surface: A drinker sneers that the works outfit at the local is a careless bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thoughtless gives no heed to others' feelings, which is exactly what being inconsiderate means.

clue.text: Sporting representatives of socialist associations

definitions.meaning: players chosen to represent their country in matches between nations
the First, Second and Third ... were federations of socialist and communist parties

explanation.definitionFit: Players capped for their country bear this name, and so did the historic worldwide federations of working-class parties.

clue.text: Was concerned about a communist

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
a Red is a communist

explanation.surface: Someone fretted over a comrade.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been concerned about something is to have minded or worried, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Maybe a piano lent by an Italian

indicators.note: maybe signals the letters could be arranged some other way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone from Italy loaned out a keyboard instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Naples is an Italian, so the demonym is an example of the broader nationality.

clue.text: Smooth years in this period

parts.note: to iron clothes is to smooth them
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: A historian says things went smoothly for years during this era.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaeological era after bronze, when tools were forged from a hard metal, is a historical period.

clue.text: Beg for quarters and free entertainment

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are two of the compass quarters
a treat is something enjoyed at someone else's expense

explanation.surface: Soldiers plead for billets and a night out on the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg someone is to plead with or implore them, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Presently a veto from abroad

parts.note: non is French for no, a refusal heard abroad

explanation.surface: Soon a foreign power will block the motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presently' here has its older sense of 'soon', not 'at present'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb means soon or shortly, the older sense of presently.

clue.text: Can he emulate the chameleon? Just so

definitions.text: Can he emulate the chameleon? Just so

parts.words: Can he emulate the chameleon? Just so
parts.note: Jeremiah asks whether a dark-skinned African can change his skin, and Kipling's Just So Stories show one doing exactly that alongside the leopard

explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's Just So Stories include How the Leopard Got His Spots, in which a man from the Horn of Africa changes his skin colour, answering the Bible's question.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure in Jeremiah and in Kipling's tale is a man from Abyssinia, whose skin changes colour like a chameleon's.

clue.text: Study in revival — job for a scout

indicators.note: the word for study is placed inside the word for revival

parts.note: a renaissance is a revival
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A scholar researching a cultural rebirth sounds like a scout's assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouting ahead to gather information about terrain or the enemy is military reconnoitring, a scout's task.

clue.text: Volte-face when Union and Navy have a fight

parts.note: TU stands for trade union
RN is the Royal Navy
a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A sudden reversal of policy when a trade union and the Navy come to blows.
explanation.definitionFit: A volte-face is a complete reversal of opinion or policy, a synonym for a sudden about-turn.

clue.text: Yellow metalliferous aggregate round the church

indicators.note: the mineral word goes round the church abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: ore is rock containing metal
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Gold-bearing rock is found around the parish church.
explanation.definitionFit: This earthy pigment is a yellowish-brown colour, so it names a shade of yellow.

clue.text: Starts to run out down every outlet from the horse show

indicators.note: starts to these words means take the opening letter of each one

explanation.surface: Horses bolt and run out through every gate at the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy contest with bronco riding and roping is a show featuring horses.

clue.text: But surely more than four of them in a bar?

definitions.text: But surely more than four of them in a bar?

parts.words: But surely more than four of them in a bar?
parts.note: a pub's public bar was once called by a name recalling beer sold at fourpence a quart, yet any bar stocks more than four kinds of beer

explanation.walkthrough: The four-ale bar was the British name for a pub's cheapest public bar, after beer once priced at fourpence a quart.
explanation.definitionFit: Beers served in pubs; the four-ale bar was named after them, though a bar surely sells more than four.

clue.text: Game played in the river, see

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
lo is an old word for see or behold

explanation.surface: A match staged in the water, look.
explanation.definitionFit: A game played on horseback with mallets and a ball is one sport among many games.

clue.text: Satan, the arch-enemy (perhaps it isn't "arch")

indicators.note: perhaps hints the quoted letters might be arranged otherwise, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: The Devil is the great foe, though maybe he is not mischievous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges IT ISN'T ARCH; the surface plays on 'arch' meaning mischievous rather than chief.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian belief the great opponent of Christ is a devilish figure identified with the Devil.

clue.text: Queen of the Belgians, note, with colossal standing

parts.note: Astrid was Queen of the Belgians, wife of Leopold III
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Belgium's queen, observe, had a towering reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Colossus of Rhodes was said to stand with legs spanning the harbour mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colossus stood with one leg on each side of the harbour, legs apart in that straddling posture.

clue.text: Poor autos, sure, from this outfit

indicators.note: poor suggests something badly made, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Shabby cars, certainly, from this firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen for her marriage is an outfit, a wardrobe.

clue.text: Strain uses notes in transposition

indicators.note: transposition means the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A musical piece is strained when its notes are moved into a different key.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain is stress or tautness, and so is its synonym for something pulled tight.

clue.text: One thus counters pressures on these lines

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means thus
bars are counters where drinks are served

explanation.surface: Someone thus resists pressures along these lines.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map, lines join places of equal atmospheric pressure, so the pressures sit on them.

clue.text: Put up prizes for each plug

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word for prizes is written upwards

parts.note: pots are trophies or prizes
per means for each

explanation.surface: Someone offers rewards for every bung.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug blocks a hole, as does a cork or bung.

clue.text: Honour one opponent with wine

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British award
I is the Roman numeral one
an anti is someone opposed

explanation.surface: A toast to an adversary, raising a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A red from Tuscany is a type of wine.

clue.text: Swindle completed? Overlook it

parts.note: a con is a swindle
done means finished or completed

explanation.surface: The fraud is finished; let it pass.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook an offence is to forgive it tacitly, letting it pass.

clue.text: No bearing needed to follow this

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: No direction is required if you just go straight ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'follow your nose' is to go straight on without any particular direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of following one's nostrils' owner means going straight ahead, with no compass heading.

clue.text: Palindromic time

indicators.note: palindromic means the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a particular time of day.

clue.text: Drug is half mumbo-jumbo

indicators.note: is half means only the first half of the phrase is kept

parts.note: ...-pocus is mumbo-jumbo, trickery

explanation.surface: This narcotic is partly nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to drug someone, especially to stupefy them by putting something in a drink.

clue.text: "Fain would I — " (Raleigh)

parts.note: Raleigh scratched on a window a line beginning with these words, saying he would rise but feared to fall

explanation.walkthrough: Raleigh's line was 'Fain would I climb, yet fear I to fall'; Elizabeth I is said to have replied 'If thy heart fails thee, climb not at all'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Raleigh's couplet completes his wish to ascend at court, despite fearing a fall.

clue.text: One not free to provide sport for seaside boarders, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: surf is what people on surfboards ride at the beach

explanation.surface: A man unable to leave offers waves for the beach crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal labourer bound to the land was unfree, tied to his lord.

clue.text: Story about, for instance, a lord

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a fib

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation for for instance is turned round

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: Tales about a nobleman, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal superior to whom vassals owe allegiance is a lord.

clue.text: Expert has foresight to make a stipulation

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
vision is foresight, the ability to plan ahead

explanation.surface: A specialist with foresight sets a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause in a contract setting a condition is a stipulation.

clue.text: Memorable? Not after bugle medley

indicators.note: a medley is a jumble, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A bugler's mixed-up tune may be hard to forget, or perhaps not.
explanation.definitionFit: Something memorable cannot easily slip from the mind.
